No unit tests exist for the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable hooks, leaving folder metadata permission model, skipToken handling, provisioned/plugin-provided rule immutability, and silence support untested

Tests covering the 'Creating'/'Deleting' state (ruler-only and prom-only propagation windows) were deleted with no replacement, so the behavior that rules with no prom counterpart vanish from the list is untested
Federated-rule support dropped in useAllRulerRuleAbilities (isFederated = false with TODO) without a test flagging the regression that federated rules are now editable/removable
GrafanaGroupLoader More-menu test only runs with all permissions granted; no negative test that Silence/Duplicate/Export/Delete are hidden when folder permissions are denied

GrafanaGroupLoader permission-denied test only overrides AlertingRuleUpdate/AlertingRuleDelete and would pass even if the hook consulted only global permissions, so folder-level metadata (hasPermissionInMetadata) behavior isn't pinned down
Dead mock setup (mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility) in RulesTable Grafana test blocks is misleading — the test asserts mock wiring rather than component logic due to the module being mocked wholesale

Federated-rule handling silently dropped: isFederated hardcoded to false in useAllRulerRuleAbilities instead of calling isFederatedRuleGroup, causing federated rules to be treated as mutable (behavior regression)

Duplicated dual-source ability-resolution logic in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: copy-pasted comments, identical prometheusRuleType guard, repeated OR-together ruler/prom abilities; intent not expressed as a prop so both hooks always run
Stray '// duplicate' marker comment left in production code in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts
RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx is an acknowledged full-file copy of RuleActionsButtons.tsx kept behind a feature flag, now diverging substantially so every bugfix must be applied twice
Dead mock in RulesTable.test.tsx: useGrafanaPromRuleAbility mocked but only plural hooks are used, so the mock is never consumed
Dead 'operation' prop on GrafanaRuleListItem: no callers pass it and the code paths consuming it were deleted in the same PR; surviving RuleOperation import is dead scaffolding

AlertRuleMenu.tsx ORs two independent ability sources (canX = rulerSupported && rulerAllowed || grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed), so mismatched/loading states between the two async evaluators can show actions the authoritative source denies
GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx lost the rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused ruler fallback (pause state now wrong/stale during propagation lag) and dropped returnTo from the view href, losing navigation context

Duplicate action in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities only checks global rulesPermissions.create without folder resolution, so it stays allowed even when the rule's folder is unreadable/deleted while isEditable/isRemovable are false

Test mocks in RulesTable.test.tsx and GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx only assert permissive cases and mimic desired hook behavior, leaving no negative-matrix coverage so a regression where useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities always returns allowed would not be caught

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated rule immutability check dropped in useAllAlertRuleAbilities: isFederated is hard-coded to false with only a TODO, allowing Edit/Delete/Pause on federated rules that should be immutable

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the federated immutability logic has been effectively removed: it now sets `isFederated = false` with a TODO (and the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` check is gone), so `immutableRule` no longer accounts for federated rule groups. Since `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable` gates Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently, this change can incorrectly allow those actions on federated rules that should be immutable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Prom-only (pending-deletion) rules now render as fully normal actionable list items in GrafanaGroupLoader, showing editable/deletable rules whose backing ruler definition is gone, with the old warning telemetry removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all handling of “prom-only” rules (previously rendered via `promOnlyRules.map(...)` as a `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting`) and also removes the `matchRules()` logic that detected prom-only vs matched rules. `GrafanaGroupLoader` now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)` as `GrafanaRuleListItem`, which attaches `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` (see new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`). This means any rule that exists only in the Prom response (the prior pending-deletion case) will now appear as a normal, actionable item. Additionally, the prior warning telemetry (`logWarning(...)` inside `matchRules` when promOnlyRules existed) is deleted along with `matchRules`, matching the finding’s “warning telemetry removed” claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Just-created ruler-only rules are no longer rendered at all during ruler-to-prom propagation, so a newly created rule vanishes from the list until propagation completes

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the loader no longer queries the Ruler API (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` was removed) and no longer renders `rulerResponse?.rules` with a fallback "Creating" operation when a matching Prom rule is missing. Instead it only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`. Therefore, if a rule exists only in the Ruler response (e.g., just created and not yet present in the Prometheus groups response), it will not be rendered at all until it appears in `promResponse`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2 silently renders nothing for promRule-only cloud rules because getEditableIdentifier returns undefined for cloud prom rules with only a console warning masking the failure

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2, if only `promRule` is provided and it is not a Grafana prom rule, `getEditableIdentifier()` falls through, logs `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')`, returns `undefined`, and the component returns `null` (`if (!identifier) { return null; }`). This does mean the UI can silently render nothing for promRule-only non-Grafana rules. However, the diff does not show an actual caller passing a promRule-only *cloud* rule into this component (the new promRule-only usage shown is for GrafanaPromRuleDTO via GrafanaRuleListItem), so the specific “cloud promRule-only” runtime scenario is not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Folder-fetch failures in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable are masked as no permissions, making load failures indistinguishable from genuine permission denials with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In the new `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` helper, when `useFolder(folderUID)` yields no `folder`, the hook returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` (and if `loading` is false, it becomes an indistinguishable “no permissions” result). The surrounding `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` then treats support as `AlwaysSupported` when `loading` is false, so update/delete become “supported but not allowed” with no surfaced error. The diff shows no error channel/handling for folder-fetch failures, so a folder load failure (or invalid UID) can be masked as permission denial.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loss of returnTo query param on rule view links in GrafanaRuleListItem, so users lose filter context when navigating back from a filtered list

adjudication.rationale: The old GrafanaRuleListItem (in deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built links with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. The new `public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter, so navigation will no longer preserve the list/filter context via the returnTo query param.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OR-combining ruler and prom ability sources in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx weakens UI authorization gating (fail-open), since permission decision can come from the least restrictive source when hooks disagree, are loading, or reference different rule revisions

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes UI gating to a permissive OR across two independent ability sources. In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, canPause/canDelete/etc are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`. In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, `canEditRule` is similarly OR-combined between `useRulerRuleAbility(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. This means if the two hooks disagree (e.g., due to differing rule representations/immutability inputs such as optional `provenance` on GrafanaPromRuleDTO or different permission derivations), the UI will enable/show actions based on the more permissive result rather than failing closed. The diff doesn’t prove a concrete runtime mismatch will occur, but the “least restrictive source wins” behavior is directly present and is a legitimate review concern about authorization signaling in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In useAbilities.ts, useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false, so federated Mimir rule groups lost their immutable protection and now show Edit/Delete/Pause/Duplicate affordances previously locked

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes federated-group detection from the abilities logic. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it in `immutableRule` to disable edit/delete/etc. After the change, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and the new `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` (with a TODO). This means federated rule groups will no longer be treated as immutable by this hook, potentially re-enabling supported/allowed affordances (Edit/Delete/Pause/Duplicate) that were previously blocked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 folder fetch: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable calls useFolder(folderUID) per rule row, fanning out M getFolder requests proportional to distinct folders rendered, amplified by pagination and polling

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()`, which calls `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule)`; that function calls `useFolder(folderUID)` (new in `useAbilities.ts`). This ability hook is then used from list-row components via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities` (e.g., `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` and `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`), meaning each rendered rule row can trigger its own `useFolder(rule.folderUid)` lookup. That is a concrete per-row/per-distinct-folder fan-out pattern created by this change, which can become an N+1-style performance issue under pagination/polling (though whether it results in multiple network requests depends on `useFolder` caching, which isn't shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu unconditionally invokes both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, running ruler availability check even in prom-only list view where ruler API was removed

adjudication.rationale:
In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the component now always calls both hooks:
- useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [...])
- useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, [...])
There is a skipToken guard for the Prom rule hook, but no analogous guard for the ruler hook; useRulerRuleAbilities is invoked even when rulerRule is undefined (prom-only/list-view case). In useAbilities.ts, useRulerRuleAbilities delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier), which calls useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule) regardless of rule being undefined. The diff doesn’t show whether useIsRuleEditable performs any Ruler availability/API checks, so the claim about definitely “running ruler availability check” can’t be fully verified from the diff, but the unconditional invocation (and potential to reintroduce work/requests) is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons runs useRulerRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbility for the same rule, doubling per-row hook/query work versus old single pipeline

adjudication.rationale: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, the component now always calls both `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, ...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(promRule ? ... : skipToken, ...)` for the Update action and ORs the results (`canEditRule = ... || ...`). Previously it only used the ruler-based ability hook. This is a diff-grounded performance/architecture concern because it increases per-row hook evaluation work and may trigger additional underlying permission/editability computations (e.g., `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`/`useIsRuleEditable` plus `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useFolder`) even when one source would suffice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useMemo on actions array is ineffective because callers pass inline literal arrays, so array identity changes every render and memoization never happens

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows hooks memoizing results with `useMemo(..., [abilities, actions])` (e.g., `useRulerRuleAbilities` / `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` in `useAbilities.ts`). Call sites in this diff pass inline literal arrays for `actions`, e.g. in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`: `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...])` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...])`. Those arrays are re-created each render, so `actions` identity changes and the `useMemo` will recompute every render, making the memoization ineffective. This is a performance/efficiency concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated rule handling dropped from useAllRulerRuleAbilities/useAllAlertRuleAbilities: isFederated hardcoded to false, so federated Mimir rules incorrectly report Delete/Update as supported+allowed, a contract change for all existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the refactor of `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` removes the prior federated-rule check and hardcodes `isFederated = false` (with a TODO), whereas previously federated rules were treated as immutable (via `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)`) and thus Update/Delete were not supported/allowed. This change is diff-verifiable and will cause federated rules to be evaluated as editable/removable when permissions allow, altering existing consumer behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Creating-state rules disappear from Grafana group list: ruler group query and matchRules removed, so newly-created rules that haven't propagated to Prometheus vanish instead of showing 'Creating' state; tests deleted rather than migrated

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the ruler-group query and the matching logic that previously rendered ruler-only rules with `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}` (old `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` loop over `rulerResponse?.rules` and the `if (!promRule)` branch). The new `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and deletes `matchRules` and the “prom-only (Deleting)” list items entirely, and the related tests were removed from `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`. However, the finding’s core claim that newly-created rules will exist in the ruler API but not in the Prometheus API (and therefore “disappear”) is not something the diff can verify; it depends on backend consistency behavior outside this PR. What is verifiable is a loss of UI handling/tests for that edge-state, not a guaranteed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons returns null for cloud rules without a ruler rule: new optional rule/promRule prop with getEditableIdentifier can yield undefined, silently hiding View/Edit/Delete actions

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a `return null` path in `RuleActionsButtons.V2` when `getEditableIdentifier(...)` can’t build an identifier (i.e., no `rule`, and `promRule` is not a Grafana Prom rule). However, the diff does not show any cloud-rule call site passing `RuleActionsButtons` without a `ruler` rule. The only new/changed usage shown is `GrafanaRuleListItem`, which always passes a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(...)`), so an identifier is constructed and actions are not hidden. The claim specifically about “cloud rules without a ruler rule” is not verifiable from this PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silence ability semantics changed in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities: useCanSilence (external Alertmanager config) replaced with folder permissions + silence support check, so external-Alertmanager users may see incorrectly enabled Silence action

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the `Silence` ability is now computed as `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (via `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` and `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)`) rather than using the prior `useCanSilence(rule)` logic used for ruler rules. The diff shows this is a deliberate semantic shift for Grafana Prom rules, but the claim about “external Alertmanager users” being incorrectly enabled cannot be verified from the diff because the behavior/implementation of `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport` and the old `useCanSilence` are not shown. Still, it’s a concrete, diff-grounded concern about potentially missing a configuration-dependent gating condition for silencing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: View URL loses returnTo query parameter in GrafanaRuleListItem, regressing navigation flow so users land on default page instead of returning to the rule list

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the view link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()` to preserve the return navigation. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, the href is now `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` passed, so the returnTo query parameter is dropped by this diff, plausibly regressing the navigation flow back to the rule list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllRulerRuleAbilities signature loosened to accept rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, so isPluginProvidedRule(rule) and rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) may receive undefined and throw or mis-classify

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not loosen the signature of `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`; it already accepted `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` before (the removed implementation at the bottom shows the same signature). While the new implementation still calls `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` and `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` with a potentially `undefined` `rule`, that behavior pre-existed and the diff does not show that either helper would throw on `undefined` (their implementations aren’t in the diff). Therefore the finding’s claim that this risk is introduced by a signature change is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities skipToken only nulls the rule; the underlying useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and useFolder query still run full ability computation for non-grafana rows, so skip semantics are not honored

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `skipToken` is explicitly translated to `undefined` (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule)`), and `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` immediately treats `!rule || !folderUID` as non-editable with `loading: false`. While `useFolder(folderUID)` is still *invoked* with `folderUID` possibly `undefined`, the finding’s key claim—"the underlying ... useFolder query still run" and that skip semantics are "not honored"—cannot be verified from this diff because `useFolder`’s behavior on `undefined` is not shown. The diff does not prove that a network request or expensive computation happens for non-grafana rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useRulerRuleAbility called with possibly-undefined rule in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx because the singular hook's signature was not widened to accept optional rule, risking runtime errors in the promRule-only path

adjudication.rationale: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, `rule` was made optional via `RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule; }>` and the new `GrafanaRuleListItem` uses `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />`, so the `promRule`-only path will call `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, ...)` with `rule === undefined`. The diff does not show `useRulerRuleAbility` being updated to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` (only `useRulerRuleAbilities` was widened), so this is a concrete API-usage/type-safety issue and could become a runtime problem depending on the hook implementation, but the runtime failure itself cannot be verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader no longer surfaces query errors from useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery, showing a misleading 'did not find any rule groups' alert when the request actually failed

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery` result is destructured as `{ data: promResponse, isLoading: isPromResponseLoading }` with no `error` handling. The component then treats `!promResponse` (when not loading) as “Did not find any rule groups” and renders that Alert. With RTK Query, a failed request commonly yields `data` undefined and `error` set, so this change would surface a misleading “did not find” message on real query failures instead of an error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed intermediate-state handling in GrafanaGroupLoader: 'Creating'/'Deleting' matchRules logic was deleted, so deleting rules show with enabled action buttons and newly created rules disappear until propagation

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the dual-source reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader` (deletes `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, the `matchRules` function, and the rendering of `RuleOperation.Creating` / `RuleOperation.Deleting` items). The loader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` via `GrafanaRuleListItem`, so any previously-handled mismatch cases (ruler-only rules during creation, prom-only rules during deletion) would no longer get special UI treatment. However, the PR also removes ruler API usage in list view and appears to assume/promote strong consistency, so whether those intermediate states still occur (making this a definite bug) cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable treats folder fetch failure as 'no permission', permanently hiding Edit/Delete/Pause actions with no error, retry, or indication

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` which derives `isEditable/isRemovable` solely from `useFolder(folderUID)` but does not expose/handle any folder-fetch error state. In the `useMemo`, when `!folder` it returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` (and when `loading` becomes false while `folder` is still undefined due to a fetch failure), abilities in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` will evaluate as not allowed and thus hide Edit/Delete/Pause without any indication. This is a concrete edge-case/UX robustness issue introduced by the new hook, though the diff alone can’t prove it is always incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu runs both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities unconditionally, doubling ability/folder permission requests and OR-combining results so the more permissive source wins

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the component always calls both hooks: useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(... ? promRule : skipToken, ...). Even when promRule is not a Grafana prom rule, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still runs (it just receives skipToken), so any work done inside useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (e.g., folder/permission lookups) may still occur. The resulting permissions are then OR-combined (e.g., canDelete = (rulerDeleteSupported && rulerDeleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)), which is an architectural/performance concern and could mask mismatches between the two permission models, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete correctness/security break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inline array literals for actions in AlertRuleMenu defeat memoization of the ability hooks, causing per-render recomputation across ~80 rules × 2 hooks

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, both `useRulerRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...])` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...])` are passed inline array literals. In `useAbilities.ts`, `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` wrap the mapping in `useMemo` with dependency arrays that include `actions` (`[abilities, actions]`). Because the array literal is a new reference on every render, that memoization is defeated and the mapping recomputes per render. This is a performance concern (especially in a list rendering many rules), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: returnTo param dropped from rule link in GrafanaRuleListItem, losing 'back to filtered list' navigation context

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `returnTo` query parameter from Grafana rule links. Previously, `GrafanaRuleListItem` (in the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` now sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, and `FilterView.tsx`/`GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` now use this new component. This is a verifiable regression in preserving navigation context back to the filtered list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable tests mock the entire useAbilities module, so the new OR-combination logic (useRulerRuleAbilities / useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and gating in AlertRuleMenu.tsx / RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx) has no real coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx` the module `../../hooks/useAbilities` is mocked wholesale (`jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')`), and the tests drive behavior purely via mocked return values for `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/etc. That means the new real ability-resolution logic added in `useAbilities.ts` (e.g. `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `skipToken` handling) is not exercised by these tests—only the components’ wiring against mocked abilities is. While the OR-combination in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`/`RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` can still be executed using mocks, these RulesTable tests don’t provide integration coverage that the new hooks compute correct supported/allowed values in real scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit tests exist for the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable hooks, leaving folder metadata permission model, skipToken handling, provisioned/plugin-provided rule immutability, and silence support untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new logic in `useAbilities.ts` (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the internal `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `skipToken`, and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities`). While several component tests were updated/added (e.g., `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, `RulesTable.test.tsx`), none directly exercise these new hooks’ behavior at the hook level, and many tests mock the abilities hooks (notably in `RulesTable.test.tsx`), which bypasses key branches such as `skipToken` mapping to `undefined`, provisioned/plugin-provided immutability checks (`isProvisionedPromRule`, `isPluginProvidedRule`), and the folder-metadata permission evaluation inside `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests covering the 'Creating'/'Deleting' state (ruler-only and prom-only propagation windows) were deleted with no replacement, so the behavior that rules with no prom counterpart vanish from the list is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the logic (and tests) that handled propagation-window edge cases. In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the Ruler query + `matchRules()` mapping and the rendering of `RuleOperation.Creating` (ruler-only) and `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting` (prom-only) are deleted; the component now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`. Correspondingly, `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` deletes the tests that asserted the Creating/Deleting UI states and all `matchRules` unit tests, without adding any replacement coverage for missing-counterpart cases. Whether this is a product bug depends on the (not diff-verifiable) consistency guarantees, but the loss of edge-case handling/coverage is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated-rule support dropped in useAllRulerRuleAbilities (isFederated = false with TODO) without a test flagging the regression that federated rules are now editable/removable

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the previous federated check (`isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`) was removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`, while `immutableRule` still depends on `isFederated`. This change makes federated rules no longer treated as immutable, so they can become editable/removable if permissions allow—i.e., a behavioral regression introduced by the diff. The diff also removes the federated import, confirming the drop in support, and no compensating test is added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader More-menu test only runs with all permissions granted; no negative test that Silence/Duplicate/Export/Delete are hidden when folder permissions are denied

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the new More-menu coverage is exercised under an unconditional `beforeEach` that grants broad user permissions via `grantUserPermissions([...])` and sets folder ACLs to `true` via `setFolderAccessControl({...})`. The only negative RBAC test added denies edit (`AlertingRuleUpdate`/`AlertingRuleDelete`) and asserts the Edit button is absent, but it does not click the More menu nor assert that menu actions (Silence/Duplicate/Export/Delete) are hidden/disabled when folder permissions are denied. Given the refactor to compute menu abilities from prom-rule + folder permissions (`AlertRuleMenu` now uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), this is a specific, diff-grounded gap in tests rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader permission-denied test only overrides AlertingRuleUpdate/AlertingRuleDelete and would pass even if the hook consulted only global permissions, so folder-level metadata (hasPermissionInMetadata) behavior isn't pinned down

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the "should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions" test keeps global permissions granted (beforeEach grants AlertingRuleUpdate, etc.) but overrides folder-level access via setFolderAccessControl({ AlertingRuleUpdate: false, AlertingRuleDelete: false }). If the implementation consulted only global permissions (and ignored folder metadata), the user would still have AlertingRuleUpdate globally and the Edit button would render—causing this test to fail. Therefore the test does in fact pin down folder-level metadata behavior rather than passing under a global-only check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead mock setup (mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility) in RulesTable Grafana test blocks is misleading — the test asserts mock wiring rather than component logic due to the module being mocked wholesale

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks the entire `useAbilities` module and sets up `mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, but the diff does not include the `RulesTable` component implementation (or its rendered subcomponents) to verify whether `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` is actually unused (“dead”) in those Grafana test blocks. Also, the tests still assert rendered UI behavior (presence/absence of buttons) based on hook outputs; mocking a hooks module wholesale is common in such tests and doesn’t, by itself, mean the test only asserts mock wiring. Therefore the finding cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated-rule handling silently dropped: isFederated hardcoded to false in useAllRulerRuleAbilities instead of calling isFederatedRuleGroup, causing federated rules to be treated as mutable (behavior regression)

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts), federated handling is explicitly removed: `isFederatedRuleGroup` is no longer imported and `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` with a TODO. Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, federated rules will no longer be treated as immutable and can become editable/removable based on permissions, which is a behavioral regression relative to the prior logic that checked `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated dual-source ability-resolution logic in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: copy-pasted comments, identical prometheusRuleType guard, repeated OR-together ruler/prom abilities; intent not expressed as a prop so both hooks always run

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows dual-source ability resolution implemented in two places with near-identical patterns: AlertRuleMenu.tsx now calls both useRulerRuleAbilities(...) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...) and then ORs the results for canPause/canDelete/etc. RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx similarly adds a copy-pasted comment and uses the same prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken guard with useGrafanaPromRuleAbility, then ORs it with the ruler ability for canEditRule. In both components the hooks for both sources are invoked unconditionally (even if one is fed skipToken), which is a real duplication/architecture/perf concern introduced by this change, but not a directly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stray '// duplicate' marker comment left in production code in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inline comment `// duplicate` on the line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, but this is a minor style/nit issue (a stray comment) and not a verifiable functional defect or substantive review concern based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx is an acknowledged full-file copy of RuleActionsButtons.tsx kept behind a feature flag, now diverging substantially so every bugfix must be applied twice

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly states RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx is “just a copy of RuleActionsButtons.tsx” kept for feature-flag isolation, but this PR adds substantial new, V2-specific logic (e.g., RequireAtLeastOne props, dual ability checks via useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/skipToken, getEditableIdentifier/getIsProvisioned helpers, and early return null when identifier can’t be constructed). This increases divergence between V2 and the original, making future fixes/features likely need to be applied in two places—an architectural/maintenance concern grounded in the changes shown, not a direct functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead mock in RulesTable.test.tsx: useGrafanaPromRuleAbility mocked but only plural hooks are used, so the mock is never consumed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not prove that `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` is a dead/unconsumed mock in `RulesTable.test.tsx`. While `AlertRuleMenu` was refactored to use the plural hooks (`useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), the diff also introduces real production usage of the singular hook `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`. The `RulesTable` component implementation is not shown in the diff, so it's not verifiable whether the rendered component tree in `RulesTable.test.tsx` calls the singular hook or not. Therefore the claim that the mock is “never consumed” cannot be confirmed from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead 'operation' prop on GrafanaRuleListItem: no callers pass it and the code paths consuming it were deleted in the same PR; surviving RuleOperation import is dead scaffolding

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, the `operation?: RuleOperation` prop is defined and forwarded to `<AlertRuleListItem ... operation={operation} />`, but in this diff all visible call sites (`FilterView.tsx` and `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`) pass only `rule`, `groupIdentifier`, `namespaceName`, and `showLocation`—none pass `operation`. Additionally, the prior creating/deleting rendering paths in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` were removed. This makes `operation` appear to be unused scaffolding in the refactor, but it’s a cleanup/maintainability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skipToken conflated with undefined in useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities so callers can't distinguish 'skip' from 'no rule'; also shadows the RTK skipToken symbol

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token')` in `useAbilities.ts` and uses it in callers like `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`. However, both `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` immediately convert `skipToken` to `undefined` (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule)`), so it provides no distinct semantics vs “no rule” and does not actually skip any internal work beyond what `undefined` already does. Additionally, naming it `skipToken` risks confusion with RTK Query’s well-known `skipToken` (even if not shown imported here). This is a legitimate design/clarity issue created by the diff, but not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable mixes data access, permission logic, and a global ctx by calling ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata directly instead of going through the useAlertingAbility/getRulesPermissions seam, breaking separation of concerns and testability

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` inside `useAbilities.ts`, which fetches folder data (`useFolder`) and then performs permission checks via `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update/delete, folder)` rather than reusing the existing ability-hook seams (e.g., `useAlertingAbility`) for those edit/delete checks. This does mix data access (folder load) with permission evaluation and directly depends on a `ctx` object (defined elsewhere in the module), which is an architectural/testability concern created by the change, but not a verifiable runtime correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated = false, losing the old isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check so federated rule groups lose immutability and show enabled Delete/Edit/DeletePermanently actions

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. Inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the federated check is explicitly removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO), whereas previously `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);`. Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, hardcoding `isFederated = false` means federated rule groups will no longer be treated as immutable and can surface enabled Update/Delete/DeletePermanently abilities when they should not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2 calls singular useRulerRuleAbility with a possibly undefined rule (rule is now optional), and the singular hook was not widened to accept undefined unlike the plural version, risking a crash when accessing rule.grafana_alert unguarded

adjudication.rationale: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, props were changed so `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` is optional (`RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule }>`). However the component still unconditionally calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` before any guard/early return. In `useAbilities.ts`, only the plural hook `useRulerRuleAbilities` was widened to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`, while the singular `useRulerRuleAbility` still requires a non-optional `RulerRuleDTO`. If the component is used with only `promRule` (which the diff explicitly supports via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...skipToken...)`), `rule` will be `undefined` and this call can either fail TypeScript or crash at runtime inside the singular hook when it dereferences the rule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx deleted the ruler↔prom reconciliation (matchRules, Creating/Deleting operation items, logWarning telemetry) and renders promRules only, so in-flight rules either silently vanish (creating) or render as actionable (deleting) during propagation windows

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the ruler↔prom reconciliation logic: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx no longer queries the ruler API (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery removed), deletes matchRules() and the logWarning telemetry, and stops rendering Creating/Deleting placeholders (RuleOperationListItem + RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting blocks removed). It now renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules via <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={promRule} ...>. This means any temporary divergence between ruler and Prom results would no longer be represented (e.g., a rule present only in ruler would not render; a prom-only rule would render like a normal rule item). However, whether such propagation windows still occur is not provable from the diff alone, so the finding is a concrete edge-case/regression concern rather than a definitively demonstrated bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls isProvisionedRule(rule) (and isPluginProvidedRule) with a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, but these helpers expect RulerRuleDTO reading rule.grafana_alert.provenance, so provisioned rules evaluate as editable/deletable or throw; isProvisionedPromRule should be used instead

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` was implemented to use `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` (not `isProvisionedRule(rule)`), and `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` was extended with a `provenance?: string` field to support that. So the finding’s claim that provisioned detection still calls `isProvisionedRule` / reads `rule.grafana_alert.provenance` for `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx ORs two independent ability sources (canX = rulerSupported && rulerAllowed || grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed), so mismatched/loading states between the two async evaluators can show actions the authoritative source denies

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the new logic computes e.g. `canDelete = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` after calling both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., actions)`. This explicitly allows an action if either source says allowed, which can mask disagreements between the two permission/ability evaluators (including transient differences while one hook is still resolving data, e.g. folder permissions via `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`). The diff doesn’t prove a concrete incorrect authorization outcome, but it does introduce a real consistency/authority concern in the UI gating logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx lost the rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused ruler fallback (pause state now wrong/stale during propagation lag) and dropped returnTo from the view href, losing navigation context

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably drops `returnTo` from the Grafana rule view link. The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built `href` as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, while the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` uses `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so navigation context/back-link behavior can regress. The other part of the finding (loss of `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` fallback) is true as a code change, but the claim about propagation lag being wrong/stale isn’t directly verifiable here because the new flow no longer fetches ruler rules at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate action in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities only checks global rulesPermissions.create without folder resolution, so it stays allowed even when the rule's folder is unreadable/deleted while isEditable/isRemovable are false

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `Duplicate` is computed as `toAbility(duplicateSupported, rulesPermissions.create)` after `rulesPermissions = getRulesPermissions('grafana')`, with no folder-metadata resolution. By contrast, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` explicitly resolves `update`/`delete` via `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(..., folder)`. This makes it possible for `Duplicate` to remain allowed even when folder lookup fails (e.g., unreadable/missing folder → `isEditable/isRemovable` false) because the create permission is not checked against the rule’s folder metadata.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test mocks in RulesTable.test.tsx and GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx only assert permissive cases and mimic desired hook behavior, leaving no negative-matrix coverage so a regression where useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities always returns allowed would not be caught

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple negative-permission assertions that would fail if abilities were incorrectly always-allowed. In RulesTable.test.tsx there are explicit negative cases for Grafana rules (e.g., “Should not render Edit button for users without the update permission” and “Should not render Delete button for users without the delete permission”), driven by mocked ability hooks. In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx there is also a negative case (“should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions”) that relies on folder access control setup; a regression where useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility always returned allowed would cause this test to fail. While the tests don’t exhaustively cover all menu items under denied permissions, the finding’s claim that they “only assert permissive cases” and that such a regression “would not be caught” is contradicted by the added/updated tests.
